simple.meaning: אֶלֶף (ʼeleph) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “hence (the ox's head being the first letter of the alphabet, and this eventually used as a numeral) a thousand.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 20:16. The surrounding context includes family, commandment, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֶלֶף (H505) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אֶלֶף (ʼeleph) / H505 is traced through Genesis 20:16, Genesis 24:60, Exodus 12:37, Exodus 18:21 with generated occurrence evidence.
